items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Account info is locked while it is in place.
items.name: Account info
items.desc: Stops apps reading your name, picture, and other account details, for every account. Set by policy, so the Account info page in Privacy and security says it is managed by your organization.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. These are policies, so the Contacts, Calendar, Email, Messaging, and Tasks pages under Settings > Privacy and security are locked while they are in place.
items.name: Contacts, calendar, email, and messages
items.desc: Stops Store apps reading your contacts, appointments, mail, messages, and task lists, for every account. Set by policy, so those pages in Privacy and security say they are managed by your organization.
items.riskNote: A Store mail, calendar, or messaging app you actually use stops seeing that data, which means it shows nothing. Desktop programs - Outlook, Thunderbird - are not governed by these permissions and keep working. Undoing the option takes all five policies away together.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. These are policies, so the Phone calls and Call history pages under Settings > Privacy and security are locked while they are in place.
items.name: Phone calls and call history
items.desc: Stops apps placing calls through a paired phone or reading the call log, for every account. Set by policy, so those pages in Privacy and security say they are managed by your organization.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Notifications is locked while it is in place.
items.name: Apps reading notifications
items.desc: Stops apps reading the notifications other apps raise, which is how a companion app mirrors your alerts elsewhere, for every account. Set by policy, so the Notifications page in Privacy and security says it is managed by your organization.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > App diagnostics is locked while it is in place.
items.name: App diagnostics
items.desc: Stops one app reading which other apps are running, and their process details, for every account. Set by policy, so the App diagnostics page in Privacy and security says it is managed by your organization.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. These are policies, so the Radios and Other devices pages under Settings > Privacy and security are locked while they are in place.
items.name: Radios and unpaired devices
items.desc: Stops Store apps switching Bluetooth and Wi-Fi radios on or off, and stops them talking to nearby devices you have not paired, for every account. Set by policy, so those pages in Privacy and security say they are managed by your organization.
items.riskNote: A Store app that legitimately drives a wireless accessory - a headset utility, a fitness tracker, a game controller companion - loses the ability to find or reconnect to it until the run is undone. Desktop programs are not governed by these permissions.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Camera is locked while it is in place.
items.name: Camera
items.desc: Denies every Store app access to the camera, for every account. Desktop programs are not governed by this. Set by policy, so the Camera page in Privacy and security says it is managed by your organization.
items.riskNote: The Camera app and any Store app you use for video calls stop seeing the camera. Desktop programs like Zoom or Discord are unaffected, because this only covers Store apps, and Windows Hello face sign-in reaches the camera its own way. An app already open notices after it is restarted.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Microphone is locked while it is in place.
items.name: Microphone
items.desc: Denies every Store app access to the microphone, for every account. Desktop programs are not governed by this. Set by policy, so the Microphone page in Privacy and security says it is managed by your organization.
items.riskNote: Voice typing, Store voice-call apps, and anything using the built-in speech stack stop hearing the microphone. Desktop programs are unaffected. An app already open notices after it is restarted.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. These are policies, so the Screenshots and screen recording and Screenshot borders pages under Settings > Privacy and security are locked while they are in place.
items.name: Screenshots and screen capture
items.desc: Stops Store apps taking screenshots and recording the screen, and turning off the border that shows a capture is happening, for every account. Set by policy, so those pages in Privacy and security say they are managed by your organization.
items.riskNote: Store screen recorders and screenshot tools stop working, and so does screen sharing in any Store app - the Snipping Tool is a Store app, so expect it to be refused too. Desktop capture programs like OBS are unaffected.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Privacy and security > Voice activation, and turn wake words back on.
items.name: Wake words and voice activation
items.desc: Stops apps listening for a wake word in the background, including above the lock screen, for every account. Written the way the Voice activation switches in Settings write it, so they stay yours to turn back on.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Speech is locked while it is in place; afterwards online speech recognition can be turned back on there.
items.name: Online speech recognition
items.desc: Stops speech being sent to Microsoft. Voice typing (Win+H) stops working, because it needs online recognition; Voice access and Narrator keep working.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Text and image generation shows it as managed by your organization while it is in place.
items.name: App access to on-device AI
items.desc: Stops apps using Windows' on-device text and image generation. Set by policy, so the Text and image generation page in Privacy and security says it is managed by your organization.
